To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
female 5αR-1KO mice have adrenal suppression, impaired glucocorticoid metabolism and increased hepatic glucocortiocid accumulation, and that these mice are predisposed to develop metabolic disorders.
disruption of the 5α-reduction of steroids in females results in adrenal suppression, insulin resistance, hepatic steatostosis, and predisposition to diet-induced obesity.
female 5α-reduced mice are insulin resistant and have hepatic steatoseis, and that this may be due to increased hepatic glucocortiocoid accumulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the 5α-reduced metabolites of glucocorticoid hormones on the development of metabolic disease.
the role of the 5α-reduced androgens in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease.
understanding how sex differences in the actions of glucocorticoid and androgen hormones contribute to metabolic disease in men and women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic phenotype in female mice is not driven solely by changes in androgens.
5α-reduction of glucocorticoid androgens is essential for metabolic health in female mice.
5α-reduction of glucocorticoid is a critical determinant of metabolic homeostasis in both male and female mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
disruption of 5-α reductase in mice leads to a female phenotype with increased susceptibility to metabolic disorders.
the 5αR-KO female mouse is a useful model for the study of glucocorticoid-mediated metabolic dysfunction.
the 5αR-1KO mice are more prone to develop insulin resistance and obesity than the WT mice and this is more pronounced in females than males.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5α-reduction of androgens and glucocorticoids are important determinants of metabolic health in female mice, and that the effects on metabolism may differ between the sexes.
disruption of glucocorticoid metabolism in females predisposes to insulin resistance.
the metabolic syndrome is more severe in female mice lacking 5αR-1, compared with male mice lacking 5AR-1.
